correctness.rationale: Proof checked for \(m\ge 2\) and arbitrary distinct coordinate nodes. A vanished polynomial belongs to the node-polynomial ideal; its highest homogeneous part is divisible by \((x^2+y^2)^r\). A middle-coefficient binomial Toeplitz block is positive definite for even r and strictly accretive for odd r (then the block dimension is balanced because m is odd). This forces the highest term to vanish and proves odd-grid invertibility by induction/contradiction. For m even, the explicit difference of monic node polynomials cancels its pure holomorphic and antiholomorphic degree-m terms, yielding a real, nonzero kernel vector. Exact modular rank computations at \(m=2,\ldots,10\) with two unrelated grids agree, but are acknowledged as finite checks only. No quantitative conditioning nor pure-state failure for even m is claimed.

value.rationale: The question is the natural information-theoretically critical \(m^2\)-measurement Hermitian tomography problem for truncated Gaussian/Hermite spectrograms. A universal parity law for every possible Cartesian node configuration, explicit even-case kernel and universal odd-case invertibility reveal a structural design boundary. This is not a small numerical instance, arbitrary slice, or mere code-supported count; the infinite proof has a new Toeplitz positivity mechanism and direct signal-reconstruction implications.
